title: Otterly Brilliant: Occupational Therapy Supporting Nature-Based Health Delivery and Site Improvements

content.text: By  Esther Smith, Senior Officer, Health and Environment (North East and Yorkshire)
This blog outlines the importance of green spaces in improving health and wellbeing, with a focus on occupational therapy, while showcasing some of the amazing projects in this field.

Natural England's Strategy aims to improve health and wellbeing by enabling more people to connect with, access and benefit from nature. As part of this, we are working with NHS organisations providing expert advice and early-stage funding to help develop nature-based health initiatives.

Across the NHS, there is growing interest in nature-based approaches and therapies that support physical and mental health. High-quality green spaces can play an important role in promoting wellbeing, aiding recovery, and helping to reduce health inequalities.
Oliver Harmar, Chief Strategy Officer at Natural England, said:

Green spaces offer powerful settings for occupational therapy, supporting people to manage everyday activities whether they are recovering from illness, living with a disability, facing mental health challenges or adapting to later life. Operational colleagues across our area teams are increasingly working alongside occupational therapists as part of our health and environment programme. The examples below show how these partnerships are opening up nature to more people through their occupational therapy treatment.

The Green Therapy initiative is woven into the occupational therapy curriculum and embedded across Bradford District Care Trust more widely. It brings together health, environmental and community organisations including Aire Rivers Trust, Forestry England, Canal & River Trust, Yorkshire Dales National Park Authority, YorGreen CIC, Word Up North and Pieces Project. Two events planned for autumn 2026 will help shape the future of green therapy. A roundtable will bring together NHS organisations, universities and placement hosts to explore new opportunities, while a wider stakeholder webinar will showcase green occupational therapy projects, research and partnerships from across the country.

Together, these reflect growing momentum behind nature-based approaches in occupational therapy and the power of partnership to improve health outcomes and deepen connections between people, places and communities.
